reference.name: Re-enabling pull requests silently turns on branch deletion and changes merge defaults
reference.summary: Turning a repository's pull requests off and back on in Settings > Advanced Settings doesn't restore the previous pull request settings. While pull requests are disabled, the form shows every merge option checked and every merge style selected, so re-enabling saves those: the default merge style becomes Fast-forward only and Manually merged, Delete pull request branch after merge, and autodetect manual merge all turn on. The settings page greys these options out, rather than hiding them, while the feature is off, which tells the user they'll be kept and simply inactive; saving actually deletes them.
reference.expected: Re-enabling pull requests keeps the repository's previous pull request settings, as the greyed-out options shown while pull requests are disabled suggest, or applies the same defaults as a new repository, without silently turning on branch deletion and manual merge options.
reference.actual: A repository set to Create merge commit, with Manually merged, delete-branch-after-merge and autodetect manual merge unchecked, came back as Fast-forward only with all three checked after pull requests were disabled and re-enabled. The values stayed after reload, and a new pull request's merge confirmation used Fast-forward only with Delete Branch checked.
reproSteps: In a repository's Settings > Advanced Settings, set Default Merge Style to Create merge commit, uncheck Manually merged, Delete pull request branch after merge by default and Enable autodetect manual merge, and save.
Uncheck Enable Repository Pull Requests and save.
Check Enable Repository Pull Requests again, save, and reload.
Compare the pull request settings with the ones saved in the first step.
